thread:
kai: Noticed a sudden rise in fncall/tool validation rejects for route `customer-responder` in eu-west at ~13:07 UTC. Customers see tool errors and our billing dash shows token churn. https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/validators :confused:

emma: Numbers?

kai: Quick tail:
```
validator.rejects{route=\"customer-responder\",region=\"eu-west\"} = 640 (5m)
fallback.model_fallback{route=\"customer-responder\"} = 590 (5m)
tokens.extra_burn{acct=acct-101} = +9% (15m)
```

paul: Any recent rollout changes? I thought strict-fncall-validate was gated to 10% in prod.

ops-bot: rollout.change: user=ci-agent promoted strict-fncall-validate region=eu-west percent=100 -> 13:03:12 UTC

emma: Whoa promoted to 100%? That must be automation gone wrong. :eyes:

paul: That explains it. We need a mitigation path: revert rollout or soften enforcement per-route. Which is faster?

sre-jo: Per-route soften is faster. Revert touches multiple clusters. We can flip route policy to `soft-flag` so responses return but we emit detailed telemetry and an `x-redwood-validation: soft_warning` header.

kai: Do it then. Also capture top reasons and validator version with tags. Right now dashboards only show counts and it's useless for triage.

paul: Command to flip:
`redwoodctl validators set --route customer-responder --region eu-west --policy soft-flag --note "emergency soften after accidental promotion"`

ops-bot: validators.update: route=customer-responder region=eu-west policy=soft-flag requested_by=paul 13:11:46 UTC

emma: Telemetry asks: add tags `validator_sha`, `reject_reason` (schema_mismatch|enum_invalid|missing_required), and `soft_vs_hard`. Also publish `reject_rate` as rejects/requests with 1m granularity.

paul: Agreed. We also need a derived billing metric `tokens_wasted_by_fallbacks` so billing can alert early.

console-z: UX request: Console should show per-route validator policy and an audit trail entry for any policy change (actor + diff + timestamp + reason). Also add a small "simulate payload" modal where support can paste an example and see annotated failures. That'll cut down tickets.

emma: For safety, add an automated guard: disallow promotions >10% without human_approval flag. File infra ticket.

paul: I'll file INF-10220 (automation guard), INF-10221 (telemetry tags + reject_rate metric), INF-10222 (console: policy pill + simulate modal). Assigning INF-10221 -> emma, INF-10222 -> console-z, INF-10220 -> ops team.

emma: One more idea: implement a three-state per-route policy `enforce|soft-flag|permissive` and make alerts only fire for `enforce` rejects (page on hard_reject_rate > 0.05 for 5m). Soft-flag should surface in dashboards but not trigger paging or billing alarms.

paul: Good. Also add sampling (n samples/min) for attached examples to S3 and redact PII. Keep sample size small (max 400 bytes).

sre-jo: For longer-term: consider a hybrid soft-reject response that returns the tool output but includes a structured `validation` field in the JSON with reasons and a confidence score. Emits metric and keeps user experience intact.

kai: Nice. Let's prioritize telemetry and the automation guard first. Emma, can you wire up the `reject_rate` panel and a top-5 `reject_reason` breakdown? Paul, can you do the policy flip audit UI?

emma: On it. Will add a dashboard: reject_rate, fallback_rate, tokens_wasted_by_fallbacks, top reject reasons, 1m granularity. Alert rule for enforce-mode only.

console-z: I'll prototype the policy pill + simulate modal behind a feature flag. Low-risk.

paul: ops, please triage INF-10220 and patch promotion scripts to respect `human_approval_required` meta.

ops-bot: ticket.created INF-10220 INF-10221 INF-10222

kai: Thanks team. We'll keep the soft-flag in place while we triage samples. If this impacts billing for customers we will publish an incident update. :handshake:
